This compound is identified as a target of alpha-Fenchyl acetate and [(1E,6R,7R,8S)-6,7-dihydroxy-5-methylidene-8-propan-2-ylcyclodecen-1-yl]methyl acetate, both of which are known to interact with the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein. The scores for these interactions are consistent, indicating a plausible biological pathway. The mechanism involves the compound acting as a substrate or inhibitor of an organic anion transporter, which is a key player in the transport of various molecules, including those involved in immune function and cellular homeostasis. The evidence supports a functional link between the compound and the Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein, though the exact role of the compound in this pathway remains to be fully elucidated.
